clue.text: Act as vicar maybe, providing church with a set of holy books

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a collection of the Bible's later books

explanation.surface: A parish clergyman's supplies: a church and a set of scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar, among others, may intone or sing liturgy, so chanting is something a priest does as an example.

clue.text: Club hit — accompaniment to fish just cooked?

parts.note: chips are the standard partner of fried fish in Britain
food straight from the pan is hot

explanation.surface: A golf stroke, then a question about fresh fish-and-chips.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a lofted short approach to the green is called by this name, a kind of stroke.

clue.text: A story, nipper's prime requirement, had to be off-putting

parts.note: a story is a fib, a lie

indicators.note: the prime part is the initial letter of the word

parts.note: had, as in had a meal, means ate

explanation.surface: A tale that a child mainly needed had to be unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate is to estrange or repel people, so to be off-putting to them.

clue.text: Host's moderately tipsy — we've heard that so many times before!

definitions.text: we've heard that so many times before!

indicators.note: a tipsy person staggers, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: Guests grumble that their host is a bit drunk again, a familiar tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom said wearily of a repeated, predictable situation or excuse.

clue.text: One's got on in an endeavour to go with the flow

definitions.text: One's got on in an endeavour to go with the flow

parts.words: One's got on in an endeavour to go with the flow
parts.note: people 'jump on' this vehicle when they follow a popular trend, so it is something got on to go with the crowd

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like boarding a boat on a river; the 'flow' is fashionable opinion and the vehicle is the one in the idiom about joining a popular cause.
explanation.definitionFit: To jump on the bandwagon is an idiom for joining a trend once it is popular, i.e. going along with the majority.

clue.text: Dress up and talk big

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: garb is clothing

explanation.surface: Getting dressed up and boasting.
explanation.definitionFit: To brag is to boast, which is what talking big means idiomatically.

clue.text: International organisation to protect old city: way one can make people feel better?

definitions.text: one can make people feel better?

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so the city sits within the organisation

parts.note: NATO, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city
a path is a way

explanation.surface: NATO guarding an ancient city as a route to cheering people up.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturopath treats illness through natural remedies, a practitioner who aims to heal patients.

clue.text: Upcoming fashion — chain of shops to provide special footwear

parts.note: welling up is coming up, as tears do
ton is an old word for fashion or style
Boots is a UK chain of chemist's shops

explanation.surface: A trendy new fashion from a high-street chain.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots is a British pharmacy chain; 'the ton' means high fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: These are rubber waterproof boots, named after the Duke, a particular kind of footwear.

clue.text: Periodical served up piece as a good opener?

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: mag, short for magazine
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A magazine runs an article meant as a strong introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambit is an opening move in chess, or any opening remark intended to gain an advantage.

clue.text: No worry with energy at a minimum in early period

indicators.note: at the lowest point, i.e. at the bottom of this down entry

parts.note: taken as written
to nag is to worry or pester
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Untroubled and low on energy during one's youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonage is the time of being under legal age, i.e. youth or immaturity.

clue.text: One "spiky" type to go off the deep end, rambling

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a tine is a prong or spike, e.g. of a fork or antler
to go off the deep end is to lose one's temper, i.e. to rant

explanation.surface: Someone prickly who flies into a temper while wandering about.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerant person travels from place to place, so the adjective matches wandering or roving.

clue.text: Buggy feasible for bringing fruit

parts.note: LEM is the Lunar Excursion Module, the Apollo moon craft, loosely a moon buggy
something 'on' is possible or doable, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: A pushchair being practical for carrying fruit home from the shops.
explanation.definitionFit: The lemon is a sour yellow citrus fruit, an example of the class named.

clue.text: Formula for making little Sarah's shoe

indicators.note: a formula is a recipe, so the clue asks for the recipe that produces the short name, written out in words

parts.note: Sal is a pet form of Sarah, built from her name's first letter and last two letters with a joining word between

explanation.surface: A recipe for producing a child's shoe called Sarah's.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Sarah is SAL; the formula for making it is 'S and AL', which run together spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandal is an open shoe held on with straps, a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Trying hard, not having succeeded in the gym?

indicators.note: the instruction says the following letter must be absent from the word just found

parts.note: straining is making a great effort
s. is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: Someone sweating away at the gym without results.
explanation.walkthrough: In family trees 's.' stands for 'succeeded'; drop it from STRAINING.
explanation.definitionFit: What people do at a gym is train, exercising to improve fitness, so they are training there.

clue.text: County and country inadequately supplied with money — anger ensues

indicators.note: falling short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a land is a country
cash is money
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A nation short of funds and rising fury as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancashire is a county in north-west England.

clue.text: Exceptional man with great hope campaigning very vigorously?

indicators.note: exceptional suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters of these words are rearranged into an unusual order

explanation.surface: A remarkable candidate with high hopes fighting an energetic election campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the rampage means rushing about wildly and violently, the playful sense being a frenzied campaigner.

clue.text: Dog left out in the open given drink at the pub

parts.note: aired, as washing hung outside
ale is a beer

explanation.surface: A dog left outside while its owner drinks in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed from Yorkshire.

clue.text: Pieces of sculpture mostly standing on a pair of parallel lines

indicators.note: most of the word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: status is standing or rank
RY is short for railway, two rails side by side

explanation.surface: Statues standing beside a railway track.
explanation.definitionFit: Statuary is sculptures collectively, a group of statues.

clue.text: Notice lout is on the loose — I will speak out in a clear manner

definitions.text: I will speak out in a clear manner

indicators.note: something on the loose is running free and out of control, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A warning that a hooligan has escaped, followed by a vow to speak up clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: An elocutionist is a teacher or practitioner of clear, correct diction, here speaking about themself in the first person.

clue.text: Char and whisky, when time is right

indicators.note: time becoming right, so one letter is changed for another

parts.note: Scotch is whisky

explanation.surface: Tea and a whisky at the proper hour.
explanation.walkthrough: Char looks like the British slang for tea, but it is the verb to burn.
explanation.definitionFit: To char is to burn and blacken a surface, which scorching also does.

clue.text: Worker in study somewhere in Switzerland?

indicators.note: the insect sits inside the study word

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
the worker ant is the crossword stock worker

explanation.surface: An employee in a study room somewhere in the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: Switzerland is divided into cantons, its federal states, so a canton is a region there.

clue.text: Most idiotic fools, right to the fore, in court

indicators.note: the combined letters sit within the abbreviation for court
says the letter for right goes at the front of the fools

parts.note: asses are foolish people

explanation.surface: The stupidest fools being pushed to the front in a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass means grossly stupid or insensitive, so its superlative is the most stupid.

clue.text: Miserable aim to get new leader

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is swapped for another, giving it a new head

parts.note: an object is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: An unhappy ambition that needs someone fresh in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The new first letter is not clued; the change from O to A is fixed by the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Abject describes a wretched, hopeless state, as in abject poverty, close to wretched.

clue.text: An item or two?

definitions.meaning: a romantic couple is called an item

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks about one thing or two; 'item' is the slang for a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple dating is 'an item', and any set of two of a kind is likewise a couple.

clue.text: Maybe one-to-one operation is somewhat lacking

indicators.note: the word is shorn of some of its letters, leaving a stretch from within it

parts.note: the letters are found inside this single word

explanation.surface: An operation that falls a bit short.
explanation.walkthrough: Take 'operation' and lose its outer bits to leave the middle five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses a relation between quantities, one-to-one being an example.

clue.text: Soon despicable fellow gets a woman to have close relationship

parts.note: in a mo (in a moment) means soon
a rat is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A cad is about to win over a lady for an intimate affair.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a female lover, the woman someone is romantically involved with.

clue.text: Description of Winnie as a mammal?

definitions.meaning: Winnie the Pooh is a bear devoted to honey
the kinkajou or the sun bear goes by this name

explanation.walkthrough: Winnie is Winnie the Pooh, A. A. Milne's honey-loving teddy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase fits Pooh's ruling passion and is also a real name for an animal species.

clue.text: Scruffy children — last thing academy needs

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Untidy pupils are the last thing a school wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedy means shabby and run-down, close to scruffy in appearance.
